seoTitle: HAProxy Log Parser: Timers and Termination State Codes
metaDescription: Decode HAProxy httplog lines: Tq/Tw/Tc/Tr/Ta timers, status and the four-letter termination state explained in words. Free.
intro: Parses HAProxy HTTP logs and explains termination flags such as sH-- and SC--.
why:
The termination state shows why a session ended: a client abort, a server timeout, a refused connection. It is the fastest way to tell a slow backend from a dead one, but the letters are hard to remember.

The first two letters are decoded from the HAProxy configuration manual, section 8. Timers are in milliseconds and -1 means the stage was not reached.
howTo: Paste httplog lines from syslog or haproxy.log.
Check timers and queue waits in the table.

faq.a: The request was aborted before a full request arrived.
No. Only the first two letters. The third and fourth are shown as written.

faq.q: What if some lines do not match?
faq.a: They are skipped and the result says how many. TCP-mode and custom log-format lines are not supported.
No. Everything is processed in your browser and nothing is sent. Logs can hold IP addresses and tokens, so the page does not write them into the address bar.
